Introduction to DBMS & SQL Server

days.the8020Knowledge: Databases organize data into 8KB physical storage pages grouped into 64KB extents. Write operations hit the transaction log (.ldf) first before committing to data files (.mdf), guaranteeing ACID reliability.
days.whatExpertsUnderstand: Understanding page allocation and log file write-ahead logging (WAL) separates database developers from casual query writers. It explains checkpoint overhead, transaction log growth, and query I/O cost.

topicExplanation.whatIsIt: A Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) is structured software that stores, retrieves, and enforces integrity on business data using relational tables with rows and columns.
topicExplanation.whyLearnIt: Every enterprise data platform, data pipeline in Azure, and Power BI report ultimately ingests data originating from relational databases.
coreConcepts: Drawbacks of File Management Systems (data redundancy, lack of concurrency, zero integrity enforcement)

SQL Server Architecture: Protocol Layer, Relational Engine (Query Parser, Optimizer), Storage Engine (Buffer Pool, Access Methods)
Connecting to Server & Authentication Modes: Windows Integrated Authentication (Kerberos/NTLM) vs Mixed Mode SQL Authentication

practiceTask.instructions: Connect to your SQL Server instance in SSMS, create a database named 'CorporateDW' specifying initial size 50MB and autogrowth 64MB for data, and 25MB for log. Inspect database properties.
acceptanceCriteria: Database CorporateDW created successfully with dedicated .mdf and .ldf files
Autogrowth configured to sensible size chunks (not 1MB)
Verified files in sys.database_files catalog view
practiceTask.validation: Run: SELECT name, size*8/1024 AS SizeMB, growth, is_percent_growth FROM sys.database_files;

codeExample.title: Creating Database with Custom File Architecture
codeExample.code:
CREATE DATABASE CorporateDW
ON PRIMARY (
    NAME = CorporateDW_Data,
    FILENAME = 'C:\SQLData\CorporateDW.mdf',
    SIZE = 50MB,
    MAXSIZE = 5GB,
    FILEGROWTH = 64MB
)
LOG ON (
    NAME = CorporateDW_Log,
    FILENAME = 'C:\SQLLog\CorporateDW.ldf',
    SIZE = 25MB,
    MAXSIZE = 1GB,
    FILEGROWTH = 32MB
);
codeExample.explanation: Explicitly sets initial file sizes and fixed megabyte autogrowth to prevent Virtual Log File fragmentation.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between a page and an extent in SQL Server?
interviewQuestions.answer: A page is the fundamental unit of data storage in SQL Server, sized at 8 KB. An extent is a collection of eight physically contiguous pages (64 KB). SQL Server allocates storage in extents.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Tests whether the candidate understands internal storage architecture rather than just surface-level SQL syntax.

interviewQuestions.question: Why should data files (.mdf) and transaction log files (.ldf) be separated physically in production?
interviewQuestions.answer: Data file operations are predominantly random I/O (reads and checkpoint writes), whereas transaction log operations are strictly sequential writes. Placing them on separate storage drives avoids I/O head contention and guarantees write-ahead logging performance.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Evaluates production database administration awareness.

quiz.question: What is the physical size of a single data page in Microsoft SQL Server?
quiz.explanation: SQL Server data pages are fixed at 8 KB (8192 bytes). Eight contiguous pages form a 64 KB extent.

quiz.question: Which file extension is traditionally used for SQL Server secondary data files?
quiz.explanation: .mdf is the primary data file, .ldf is the transaction log file, and .ndf is for secondary data files.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the transaction log (.ldf)?
options: Records all database modifications before they are written to data files for ACID recovery
quiz.explanation: The transaction log enables write-ahead logging (WAL), guaranteeing durability and point-in-time recovery.

Learn the difference between 8KB pages and 64KB extents
Connect to SQL Server via Windows & SQL Authentication in SSMS
Inspect database properties and file configuration
revisionQuestions: What are the four components of ACID properties in databases?

days.studyGuideText:
================================================================================
AEROLEARN OS | DAILY LEARNING OPERATING SYSTEM
DAY 1: Database Fundamentals, DBMS Types & SQL Server Architecture
Module: Module 1: Relational Database Architecture & SQL Server / T-SQL
Authoritative PDF Citation: Azure Data Engineering (page 9), Data Analytics Using Power BI (page 14)
Recommended Duration: 4 hours
================================================================================

1. WHAT IS THIS TOPIC & WHY IT MATTERS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) is structured software that stores, retrieves, and enforces integrity on business data using relational tables with rows and columns.

Why You Must Learn It:
Every enterprise data platform, data pipeline in Azure, and Power BI report ultimately ingests data originating from relational databases.

2. THE 80/20 RULE (KEY PRINCIPLES TO RETAIN):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> Databases organize data into 8KB physical storage pages grouped into 64KB extents. Write operations hit the transaction log (.ldf) first before committing to data files (.mdf), guaranteeing ACID reliability.

3. MEASURABLE LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [ ] Explain file management system drawbacks and the necessity of modern DBMS
  [ ] Differentiate Network, Hierarchical, and Relational (RDBMS) systems
  [ ] Configure SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and understand Windows vs. SQL Authentication
  [ ] Describe SQL Server storage internals: data files (.mdf/.ndf), log files (.ldf), pages, and extents

4. CORE SYLLABUS MECHANICS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. Drawbacks of File Management Systems (data redundancy, lack of concurrency, zero integrity enforcement)
  2. DBMS Evolution: Hierarchical (tree-based) vs Network (graph-based) vs Relational (tuple-relation based)
  3. SQL Server Architecture: Protocol Layer, Relational Engine (Query Parser, Optimizer), Storage Engine (Buffer Pool, Access Methods)
  4. Connecting to Server & Authentication Modes: Windows Integrated Authentication (Kerberos/NTLM) vs Mixed Mode SQL Authentication

5. IMPORTANT TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Storage allocation: 1 Page = 8 KB (8192 bytes); 1 Extent = 8 contiguous pages (64 KB). Mixed extents hold multiple objects; Uniform extents belong to a single object.

6. WHAT EXPERTS UNDERSTAND (PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE & SECRETS):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Understanding page allocation and log file write-ahead logging (WAL) separates database developers from casual query writers. It explains checkpoint overhead, transaction log growth, and query I/O cost.

7. REAL-WORLD PRODUCTION APPLICATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Configuring a production database storage layout on separate NVMe disk volumes for .mdf (data) and .ldf (transaction logs) to avoid disk I/O bottlenecks.

8. COMMON PITFALLS & HOW TO AVOID THEM:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WARNING: Putting both data and log files on the same disk drive, or setting transaction log autogrowth to tiny 1MB increments which causes severe virtual log file (VLF) fragmentation.

9. PRACTICAL CODE / SCRIPT IMPLEMENTATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE DATABASE CorporateDW
ON PRIMARY (
    NAME = CorporateDW_Data,
    FILENAME = 'C:\SQLData\CorporateDW.mdf',
    SIZE = 50MB,
    MAXSIZE = 5GB,
    FILEGROWTH = 64MB
)
LOG ON (
    NAME = CorporateDW_Log,
    FILENAME = 'C:\SQLLog\CorporateDW.ldf',
    SIZE = 25MB,
    MAXSIZE = 1GB,
    FILEGROWTH = 32MB
);

10. INTERVIEW PREPARATION (HIGH-YIELD QUESTIONS):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Q1 (Beginner): What is the difference between a page and an extent in SQL Server?
  Model Answer: A page is the fundamental unit of data storage in SQL Server, sized at 8 KB. An extent is a collection of eight physically contiguous pages (64 KB). SQL Server allocates storage in extents.

  Q2 (Intermediate): Why should data files (.mdf) and transaction log files (.ldf) be separated physically in production?
  Model Answer: Data file operations are predominantly random I/O (reads and checkpoint writes), whereas transaction log operations are strictly sequential writes. Placing them on separate storage drives avoids I/O head contention and guarantees write-ahead logging performance.

11. TODAY'S COMPLETION CRITERION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Deliverable: A fully configured SQL database created via T-SQL script with custom filegroup and growth settings.
Self-Check: Install SSMS, connect to a local or remote SQL Server instance, and explain the physical filegroup structure of a database.
================================================================================

days.title: SQL Server Data Types, Unicode vs Non-Unicode & Business Integrity

pdfReferences.section: SQL Server Data Types & Business Integrity
SQL Server Data Types

learningObjectives: Differentiate Unicode (NCHAR, NVARCHAR) vs Non-Unicode (CHAR, VARCHAR) and storage impact
Select optimal data types for numerical, currency, datetime, GUID, and binary data
Implement business integrity constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT, NOT NULL
Understand identity columns and surrogate key generation in relational schema design
days.the8020Knowledge: Non-Unicode (VARCHAR) uses 1 byte per character, while Unicode (NVARCHAR) uses 2 bytes per character to support international scripts. Primary Keys enforce entity integrity; Foreign Keys enforce referential integrity.
days.whatExpertsUnderstand: Choosing NVARCHAR when VARCHAR suffices doubles the memory buffer pool footprint and network serialization payload. Using INT or BIGINT identity keys instead of GUIDs for clustered keys prevents index fragmentation.

topicExplanation.whatIsIt: Data types define the storage size, format, and allowable values for column data. Business integrity constraints enforce business rules directly at the database level to prevent corrupt or orphan data.
topicExplanation.whyLearnIt: Dirty, unconstrained data in source tables causes pipeline failures in Azure Data Factory and incorrect aggregations in Power BI.
coreConcepts: Unicode (NCHAR, NVARCHAR, NVARCHAR(MAX)) vs Non-Unicode (CHAR, VARCHAR, VARCHAR(MAX))
Exact Numerics (INT, BIGINT, DECIMAL(p,s), NUMERIC) vs Approximate (FLOAT, REAL)
Temporal types: DATE, DATETIME2(p), TIME, DATETIMEOFFSET
Integrity Constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY with ON DELETE/UPDATE rules, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT
topicExplanation.importantTechnicalDetails: DECIMAL(10,2) allocates 5 bytes (10 digits total, 2 after decimal). DATETIME2(3) uses 7 bytes with 1ms precision, replacing legacy DATETIME (8 bytes with 3.33ms rounding flaw).
topicExplanation.realWorldApplication: Enforcing referential integrity between an OrderHeader and OrderDetails table so orphan line items cannot be saved without an existing order header.
topicExplanation.commonMistakes: Using FLOAT for financial balances (leading to floating-point rounding errors) instead of DECIMAL(18,2).
topicExplanation.quickRevision: VARCHAR for single-byte English text, NVARCHAR for multi-lingual text. Constraints enforce business logic natively.
topicExplanation.whatYouShouldBeAbleToDo: Design a normalized database schema with primary keys, foreign keys, check constraints, and optimal data types.

practiceTask.instructions: Create an e-commerce schema with Customers, Products, and Orders tables. Implement primary keys, auto-incrementing identity columns, foreign key constraints with cascade rules, and check constraints (e.g. Price > 0).
acceptanceCriteria: Tables created with appropriate Unicode/Non-Unicode choices
Primary and foreign key relationships successfully established
Attempted insert with invalid price or foreign key is rejected by database engine
practiceTask.validation: INSERT INTO Products (ProductName, Price) VALUES ('Test', -5.00); -- Must throw CHECK constraint violation

codeExample.title: Schema Definition with Business Integrity Constraints
codeExample.code:
CREATE TABLE Customers (
    CustomerID INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    CustomerCode VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    FullName NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    CreatedDate DATETIME2(0) DEFAULT SYSDATETIME()
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    OrderID BIGINT IDENTITY(1000,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    CustomerID INT NOT NULL,
    OrderDate DATETIME2(0) DEFAULT SYSDATETIME(),
    TotalAmount DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (TotalAmount >= 0),
    Status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Pending' CHECK (Status IN ('Pending', 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'Delivered')),
    CONSTRAINT FK_Orders_Customers FOREIGN KEY (CustomerID) REFERENCES Customers(CustomerID)
);

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between VARCHAR and NVARCHAR in SQL Server?
interviewQuestions.answer: VARCHAR stores single-byte Non-Unicode characters (ASCII/code-page), using 1 byte per character. NVARCHAR stores double-byte Unicode characters (UTF-16), using 2 bytes per character. NVARCHAR supports all international scripts, but consumes double the storage.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Checks storage awareness and character encoding fundamentals.

interviewQuestions.question: Can a table have multiple UNIQUE constraints and multiple PRIMARY KEYs?
interviewQuestions.answer: A table can have only ONE Primary Key, but it can have multiple UNIQUE constraints. Primary Keys cannot accept NULL values, while a UNIQUE constraint in SQL Server permits a single NULL value.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Tests understanding of relational integrity rules.

quiz.question: How many bytes of storage does an INT data type consume in SQL Server?
quiz.explanation: INT is a 4-byte integer spanning from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647. BIGINT consumes 8 bytes.

quiz.question: Which constraint ensures that a column does not accept duplicate values and cannot be NULL?
quiz.explanation: A Primary Key uniquely identifies each row and strictly disallows NULL values.

quiz.question: What happens when you define a column as DECIMAL(10,2)?
options: Maximum 10 digits total, with 2 digits after the decimal point
quiz.explanation: Precision (10) is the total number of digits; Scale (2) is the number of digits to the right of the decimal point.

checklist: Understand the difference between VARCHAR and NVARCHAR
Learn when to use DECIMAL vs FLOAT
Write DDL scripts with Primary, Foreign, Unique, and Check constraints
Verify constraint violation errors in SSMS
revisionQuestions: Why is DECIMAL preferred over FLOAT for financial balances?
What is the difference between a Candidate Key and a Primary Key?

days.moduleName: Module 1: Relational Database Architecture & SQL Server / T-SQL
days.title: SQL Querying Mastery: Filtering, Joins, Aggregations & Subqueries

pdfReferences.section: Queries
Queries

learningObjectives: Master logical query processing order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY
Implement all join types: INNER, LEFT/RIGHT OUTER, FULL OUTER, CROSS JOIN, and SELF JOIN
Write multi-level aggregations using GROUP BY, HAVING, and set operators (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT)
Develop correlated and nested subqueries with EXISTS and NOT EXISTS predicates
days.the8020Knowledge: Understanding the true logical processing order of SQL execution prevents 90% of beginner errors (like attempting to filter column aliases in the WHERE clause). INNER JOIN returns matches; LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows.
days.whatExpertsUnderstand: EXISTS performs short-circuit evaluation stopping at the first match, making it significantly faster than IN for subquery existence checks against large datasets.

topicExplanation.whatIsIt: Data Query Language (DQL) allows retrieving, transforming, and filtering data from multiple relational tables using mathematical set operations and predicate logic.
topicExplanation.whyLearnIt: Writing performant SQL queries is the #1 mandatory skill for data engineers and BI developers. Bad queries stall pipelines and bloat cloud data warehouse bills.
coreConcepts: Logical Query Processing Order (why SELECT executes after WHERE and GROUP BY)
Relational Joins: Inner, Left/Right Outer, Full Outer, Cross Join (Cartesian Product), Self Join
Group-level Aggregations: SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN, MAX combined with HAVING filtering
Subquery Varieties: Scalar Subqueries, Multi-row Subqueries, Correlated Subqueries, EXISTS vs IN
Set Operators: UNION (distinct) vs UNION ALL (preserves duplicates), INTERSECT, EXCEPT
topicExplanation.importantTechnicalDetails: UNION removes duplicates by sorting the combined dataset (high memory/CPU cost). UNION ALL simply concatenates result sets without sorting.
topicExplanation.realWorldApplication: Extracting customer lifetime value and latest order status by joining Customers, Orders, and Payments tables with aggregate GROUP BY logic.
topicExplanation.commonMistakes: Using HAVING instead of WHERE for row-level filters, or using IN with a subquery that might return a NULL (which causes NOT IN to return zero rows).
topicExplanation.quickRevision: Logical order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY. Use UNION ALL unless distinct deduplication is explicitly required.
topicExplanation.whatYouShouldBeAbleToDo: Write complex analytical SQL queries joining 3+ tables with filtering, aggregation, and subqueries.

practiceTask.instructions: Write a SQL query that retrieves all customers who have placed orders totaling more than $1,000 in the last 90 days. Include their total order count, total amount spent, and their latest order date. Include customers who have never placed an order using a separate query with LEFT JOIN and WHERE OrderID IS NULL.
acceptanceCriteria: Query correctly uses INNER JOIN for active spenders with GROUP BY and HAVING
Second query uses LEFT JOIN with IS NULL filter to identify inactive accounts
Zero syntax errors and properly formatted aliases
practiceTask.validation: Execute query in SSMS against seed data.

codeExample.title: Analytical Multi-Table Query with Joins & Aggregations
codeExample.code:
-- High-value customers with total spend and recent activity
SELECT 
    c.CustomerID,
    c.FullName,
    COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
    SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS TotalSpent,
    MAX(o.OrderDate) AS LastOrderDate
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, SYSDATETIME())
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FullName
HAVING SUM(o.TotalAmount) > 1000
ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;

-- Inactive customers using Anti-Join pattern
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.FullName, c.Email
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderID IS NULL;

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING in SQL?
interviewQuestions.answer: WHERE filters individual rows BEFORE any grouping or aggregation takes place. HAVING filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY operation has executed.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Checks if the candidate understands the logical execution flow of SQL.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is UNION ALL generally faster than UNION?
interviewQuestions.answer: UNION performs a distinct sort across the combined result set to identify and eliminate duplicate rows, which requires significant memory and tempdb spills. UNION ALL directly concatenates the result streams without sorting or deduplication.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Evaluates query performance awareness.

quiz.question: Which SQL clause executes first in logical query processing?
quiz.explanation: FROM is the first logical clause evaluated, identifying and joining source tables before WHERE filters rows.

quiz.question: What is the result of a CROSS JOIN between a table with 5 rows and a table with 10 rows?

AEROLEARN OS | DAILY LEARNING OPERATING SYSTEM
DAY 3: SQL Querying Mastery: Filtering, Joins, Aggregations & Subqueries
Module: Module 1: Relational Database Architecture & SQL Server / T-SQL
Authoritative PDF Citation: Azure Data Engineering (page 11), Data Analytics Using Power BI (page 16)
Recommended Duration: 5 hours
================================================================================

1. WHAT IS THIS TOPIC & WHY IT MATTERS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Data Query Language (DQL) allows retrieving, transforming, and filtering data from multiple relational tables using mathematical set operations and predicate logic.

Why You Must Learn It:
Writing performant SQL queries is the #1 mandatory skill for data engineers and BI developers. Bad queries stall pipelines and bloat cloud data warehouse bills.

2. THE 80/20 RULE (KEY PRINCIPLES TO RETAIN):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> Understanding the true logical processing order of SQL execution prevents 90% of beginner errors (like attempting to filter column aliases in the WHERE clause). INNER JOIN returns matches; LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows.

3. MEASURABLE LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [ ] Master logical query processing order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY
  [ ] Implement all join types: INNER, LEFT/RIGHT OUTER, FULL OUTER, CROSS JOIN, and SELF JOIN
  [ ] Write multi-level aggregations using GROUP BY, HAVING, and set operators (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT)
  [ ] Develop correlated and nested subqueries with EXISTS and NOT EXISTS predicates

4. CORE SYLLABUS MECHANICS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. Logical Query Processing Order (why SELECT executes after WHERE and GROUP BY)
  2. Relational Joins: Inner, Left/Right Outer, Full Outer, Cross Join (Cartesian Product), Self Join
  3. Group-level Aggregations: SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN, MAX combined with HAVING filtering
  4. Subquery Varieties: Scalar Subqueries, Multi-row Subqueries, Correlated Subqueries, EXISTS vs IN
  5. Set Operators: UNION (distinct) vs UNION ALL (preserves duplicates), INTERSECT, EXCEPT

5. IMPORTANT TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UNION removes duplicates by sorting the combined dataset (high memory/CPU cost). UNION ALL simply concatenates result sets without sorting.

6. WHAT EXPERTS UNDERSTAND (PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE & SECRETS):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXISTS performs short-circuit evaluation stopping at the first match, making it significantly faster than IN for subquery existence checks against large datasets.

7. REAL-WORLD PRODUCTION APPLICATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Extracting customer lifetime value and latest order status by joining Customers, Orders, and Payments tables with aggregate GROUP BY logic.

8. COMMON PITFALLS & HOW TO AVOID THEM:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WARNING: Using HAVING instead of WHERE for row-level filters, or using IN with a subquery that might return a NULL (which causes NOT IN to return zero rows).

9. PRACTICAL CODE / SCRIPT IMPLEMENTATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- High-value customers with total spend and recent activity
SELECT 
    c.CustomerID,
    c.FullName,
    COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
    SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS TotalSpent,
    MAX(o.OrderDate) AS LastOrderDate
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, SYSDATETIME())
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FullName
HAVING SUM(o.TotalAmount) > 1000
ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;

-- Inactive customers using Anti-Join pattern
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.FullName, c.Email
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderID IS NULL;

10. INTERVIEW PREPARATION (HIGH-YIELD QUESTIONS):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Q1 (Beginner): What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING in SQL?
  Model Answer: WHERE filters individual rows BEFORE any grouping or aggregation takes place. HAVING filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY operation has executed.

  Q2 (Intermediate): Why is UNION ALL generally faster than UNION?
  Model Answer: UNION performs a distinct sort across the combined result set to identify and eliminate duplicate rows, which requires significant memory and tempdb spills. UNION ALL directly concatenates the result streams without sorting or deduplication.

11. TODAY'S COMPLETION CRITERION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Deliverable: A collection of 5 real-world analytical SQL queries solving sales, customer churn, and inventory problems.
Self-Check: Write complex analytical SQL queries joining 3+ tables with filtering, aggregation, and subqueries.

INNER JOIN Sales.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.CustomerID;
GO

codeExample.title: Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD Type 2) Upsert Implementation
codeExample.code:
-- SCD Type 2 Implementation using MERGE & Historical Row Versioning
MERGE INTO dbo.DimCustomer AS Target
USING dbo.StagingCustomer AS Source
ON (Target.CustomerAlternateKey = Source.CustomerID AND Target.IsCurrent = 1)
WHEN MATCHED AND (Target.CustomerAddress <> Source.CustomerAddress) THEN
    -- Expire existing record
    UPDATE SET Target.IsCurrent = 0, Target.EndDate = DATEADD(DAY, -1, CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE));

-- Insert new current version with Surrogate Key
INSERT INTO dbo.DimCustomer (CustomerAlternateKey, CustomerAddress, StartDate, EndDate, IsCurrent)
SELECT 
    s.CustomerID, 
    s.CustomerAddress, 
    CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE) AS StartDate, 
    '9999-12-31' AS EndDate, 
    1 AS IsCurrent
FROM dbo.StagingCustomer s
LEFT JOIN dbo.DimCustomer d 
    ON s.CustomerID = d.CustomerAlternateKey AND d.IsCurrent = 1
WHERE d.CustomerAlternateKey IS NULL;
codeExample.explanation: Implements Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2, retaining full audit history with StartDate, EndDate, and IsCurrent flags.

codeExample.title: Pandas Data Wrangling, Window Aggregations & Outlier Detection
codeExample.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load and optimize dataframe memory footprint
df = pd.read_csv("sales_data.csv", parse_dates=["OrderDate"])
df["StoreCategory"] = df["StoreCategory"].astype("category")

# Rolling 7-day Moving Average Revenue per Store
df["Revenue_7D_MA"] = (
    df.groupby("StoreID")["Revenue"]
    .transform(lambda x: x.rolling(window=7, min_periods=1).mean())
)

# IQR Outlier Detection
Q1 = df["Revenue"].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = df["Revenue"].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1
outliers = df[(df["Revenue"] < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR)) | (df["Revenue"] > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR))]

print(f"Dataset shape: {df.shape} | Outliers identified: {len(outliers)}")
print(df.head(5))
codeExample.explanation: Executes categorical optimization, rolling window transformations, and statistical IQR anomaly detection in Pandas.

codeExample.title: Pandas Data Wrangling, Window Aggregations & Outlier Detection
codeExample.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load and optimize dataframe memory footprint
df = pd.read_csv("sales_data.csv", parse_dates=["OrderDate"])
df["StoreCategory"] = df["StoreCategory"].astype("category")

# Rolling 7-day Moving Average Revenue per Store
df["Revenue_7D_MA"] = (
    df.groupby("StoreID")["Revenue"]
    .transform(lambda x: x.rolling(window=7, min_periods=1).mean())
)

# IQR Outlier Detection
Q1 = df["Revenue"].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = df["Revenue"].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1
outliers = df[(df["Revenue"] < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR)) | (df["Revenue"] > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR))]

print(f"Dataset shape: {df.shape} | Outliers identified: {len(outliers)}")
print(df.head(5))
codeExample.explanation: Executes categorical optimization, rolling window transformations, and statistical IQR anomaly detection in Pandas.

codeExample.title: Azure ADLS Gen2 Hierarchical Namespace Ingestion
codeExample.code:
from azure.storage.filedatalake import DataLakeServiceClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

# Secure connection using Managed Identity (No hardcoded keys)
account_url = "https://enterprisestorageadls.dfs.core.windows.net"
service_client = DataLakeServiceClient(account_url=account_url, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())

file_system_client = service_client.get_file_system_client(file_system="lakehouse")
directory_client = file_system_client.get_directory_client("raw/sales/2026/10")

# Upload payload with POSIX ACL permissions
file_client = directory_client.create_file("daily_orders.parquet")
with open("daily_orders.parquet", "rb") as data:
    file_client.append_data(data, offset=0, length=data.seek(0, 2))
    file_client.flush_data(data.tell())

print("File successfully committed to ADLS Gen2 container.")
codeExample.explanation: Interacts with Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 hierarchical directories using DefaultAzureCredential.

codeExample.title: Azure Databricks PySpark & Delta Lake ACID Upsert (MERGE)
codeExample.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

# Read incoming streaming micro-batch from Silver layer
silver_stream = (
    spark.readStream.format("delta")
    .table("lakehouse.silver_transactions")
)

# Target Delta Table in Lakehouse Gold Layer
gold_table = DeltaTable.forName(spark, "lakehouse.gold_daily_sales")

def upsert_to_delta(micro_batch_df, batch_id):
    """Executes ACID MERGE INTO ensuring idempotency"""
    (
        gold_table.alias("target")
        .merge(
            micro_batch_df.alias("source"),
            "target.TransactionID = source.TransactionID AND target.StoreKey = source.StoreKey"
        )
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute()
    )

query = (
    silver_stream.writeStream
    .foreachBatch(upsert_to_delta)
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/mnt/lakehouse/checkpoints/gold_sales")
    .start()
)
codeExample.explanation: PySpark Delta Lake streaming pipeline executing an ACID MERGE INTO (Upsert) into the Gold analytics layer.

codeExample.title: Azure Databricks PySpark & Delta Lake ACID Upsert (MERGE)
codeExample.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

# Read incoming streaming micro-batch from Silver layer
silver_stream = (
    spark.readStream.format("delta")
    .table("lakehouse.silver_transactions")
)

# Target Delta Table in Lakehouse Gold Layer
gold_table = DeltaTable.forName(spark, "lakehouse.gold_daily_sales")

def upsert_to_delta(micro_batch_df, batch_id):
    """Executes ACID MERGE INTO ensuring idempotency"""
    (
        gold_table.alias("target")
        .merge(
            micro_batch_df.alias("source"),
            "target.TransactionID = source.TransactionID AND target.StoreKey = source.StoreKey"
        )
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute()
    )

query = (
    silver_stream.writeStream
    .foreachBatch(upsert_to_delta)
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/mnt/lakehouse/checkpoints/gold_sales")
    .start()
)
codeExample.explanation: PySpark Delta Lake streaming pipeline executing an ACID MERGE INTO (Upsert) into the Gold analytics layer.

codeExample.code:
-- Azure Synapse Dedicated SQL Pool: HASH Distributed Fact Table

    SalesOrderNumber VARCHAR(25) NOT NULL,
    CustomerKey INT NOT NULL,
    ProductKey INT NOT NULL,
    OrderDateKey INT NOT NULL,
    SalesAmount DECIMAL(18,4) NOT NULL
)
WITH (
    DISTRIBUTION = HASH(CustomerKey), -- 60 distribution boundaries
    CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX,
    PARTITION (OrderDateKey RANGE RIGHT FOR VALUES (20250101, 20260101, 20270101))
);
GO
-- Replicated distribution for Dimension tables to eliminate Data Movement Service (DMS) shuffle
CREATE TABLE Analytics.DimStore (
    StoreKey INT NOT NULL,
    StoreName NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
)
WITH (
    DISTRIBUTION = REPLICATE,
    CLUSTERED INDEX (StoreKey)
);

codeExample.title: Power BI DAX: CALCULATE & Time Intelligence Formulas
codeExample.code:
-- DAX Measures for Executive Business Intelligence

-- 1. Base Revenue Measure
Total Sales = SUM(FactSales[SalesAmount])

-- 2. DAX CALCULATE overriding filter context
Total Sales All Regions = 
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales], 
    ALL(DimGeography[Region])
)

-- 3. Time Intelligence Year-To-Date
Total Sales YTD = 
TOTALYTD(
    [Total Sales], 
    DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]
)

-- 4. Period-over-Period Growth %
YoY Sales Growth % = 
VAR CurrentSales = [Total Sales YTD]
VAR PriorYearSales = CALCULATE([Total Sales YTD], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]))
RETURN
    DIVIDE(CurrentSales - PriorYearSales, PriorYearSales, 0)
codeExample.explanation: High-performance DAX measures using CALCULATE, ALL, TOTALYTD, and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR with variable optimization.

codeExample.title: Power BI DAX: CALCULATE & Time Intelligence Formulas
codeExample.code:
-- DAX Measures for Executive Business Intelligence

-- 1. Base Revenue Measure
Total Sales = SUM(FactSales[SalesAmount])

-- 2. DAX CALCULATE overriding filter context
Total Sales All Regions = 
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales], 
    ALL(DimGeography[Region])
)

-- 3. Time Intelligence Year-To-Date
Total Sales YTD = 
TOTALYTD(
    [Total Sales], 
    DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]
)

-- 4. Period-over-Period Growth %
YoY Sales Growth % = 
VAR CurrentSales = [Total Sales YTD]
VAR PriorYearSales = CALCULATE([Total Sales YTD], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]))
RETURN
    DIVIDE(CurrentSales - PriorYearSales, PriorYearSales, 0)
codeExample.explanation: High-performance DAX measures using CALCULATE, ALL, TOTALYTD, and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR with variable optimization.

1. WHAT IS THIS TOPIC & WHY IT MATTERS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Power Query ETL: Column & Row Transformations, M Code & Query Merging provides the essential enterprise capability for Power Query Editor, Advanced Editor (M Language), Split/Merge columns, Pivot/Unpivot, Group By, Append Queries, Merge Queries (Join Kinds).

Why You Must Learn It:
It is an authoritative requirement in modern cloud data platforms and business intelligence stacks, directly cited in the curriculum syllabus.

2. THE 80/20 RULE (KEY PRINCIPLES TO RETAIN):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> Focus on mastering Power Query Editor and  Advanced Editor (M Language). 80% of daily engineering tasks rely on these fundamental mechanics.

3. MEASURABLE LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [ ] Understand the core architecture and purpose of Power Query ETL: Column & Row Transformations, M Code & Query Merging
  [ ] Explain Power Query Editor and how it is applied in production
  [ ] Implement practical examples avoiding common beginner pitfalls
  [ ] Answer interview questions testing theoretical and scenario-based knowledge of this topic

4. CORE SYLLABUS MECHANICS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. Power Query Editor
  2. Advanced Editor (M Language)
  3. Split/Merge columns
  4. Pivot/Unpivot
  5. Group By
  6. Append Queries
  7. Merge Queries (Join Kinds)

5. IMPORTANT TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Standard syntax, properties, configuration parameters, and execution lifecycle associated with Power Query Editor.

6. WHAT EXPERTS UNDERSTAND (PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE & SECRETS):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Production experts prioritize maintainability, cost efficiency, and partition pruning when designing solutions around Power Query ETL: Column & Row Transformations, M Code & Query Merging.

7. REAL-WORLD PRODUCTION APPLICATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Implemented in real enterprise pipelines to automate processing, guarantee data quality, and power executive dashboards.

8. COMMON PITFALLS & HOW TO AVOID THEM:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WARNING: Neglecting resource allocation, failing to handle edge cases or null values, and bypassing proper error logging.

9. PRACTICAL CODE / SCRIPT IMPLEMENTATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- DAX Measures for Executive Business Intelligence

-- 1. Base Revenue Measure
Total Sales = SUM(FactSales[SalesAmount])

-- 2. DAX CALCULATE overriding filter context
Total Sales All Regions = 
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales], 
    ALL(DimGeography[Region])
)

-- 3. Time Intelligence Year-To-Date
Total Sales YTD = 
TOTALYTD(
    [Total Sales], 
    DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]
)

-- 4. Period-over-Period Growth %
YoY Sales Growth % = 
VAR CurrentSales = [Total Sales YTD]
VAR PriorYearSales = CALCULATE([Total Sales YTD], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]))
RETURN
    DIVIDE(CurrentSales - PriorYearSales, PriorYearSales, 0)

10. INTERVIEW PREPARATION (HIGH-YIELD QUESTIONS):
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Q1 (Intermediate): How does Power Query Editor work in production and what problem does it solve?
  Model Answer: Power Query Editor solves data processing latency, architectural complexity, and integrity issues by providing standard framework capabilities.

  Q2 (Advanced): What are the common trade-offs and performance considerations when using  Advanced Editor (M Language)?
  Model Answer: Key trade-offs include compute overhead, memory utilization, I/O serialization, and network transfer costs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

codeExample.title: Power BI DAX: CALCULATE & Time Intelligence Formulas
codeExample.code:
-- DAX Measures for Executive Business Intelligence

-- 1. Base Revenue Measure
Total Sales = SUM(FactSales[SalesAmount])

-- 2. DAX CALCULATE overriding filter context
Total Sales All Regions = 
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales], 
    ALL(DimGeography[Region])
)

-- 3. Time Intelligence Year-To-Date
Total Sales YTD = 
TOTALYTD(
    [Total Sales], 
    DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]
)

-- 4. Period-over-Period Growth %
YoY Sales Growth % = 
VAR CurrentSales = [Total Sales YTD]
VAR PriorYearSales = CALCULATE([Total Sales YTD], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey]))
RETURN
    DIVIDE(CurrentSales - PriorYearSales, PriorYearSales, 0)

/*
dtexec.exe /f "C:\SSISPackages\EnterpriseETL.dtsx" ^
           /conf "C:\SSISPackages\ProductionConfig.dtsConfig" ^
           /rep EWCDI
*/
